findings.defect: Readable collection declarations were treated as an obligation to include records created after the selected stage. This enforced subsequent-stage data in earlier handoffs.
findings.basis: User recovery amendment section 2 requires subsequent-stage information exclusion; base specification section 10 separately prohibits performing later-stage work.
findings.correction: Origin and transitive-provenance boundary expectations; 50 actual external prompt builds and 16 non-external rejections; no silent prompt-builder skip.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED SYNTHETIC ROUTE CASES PASS

findings.defect: The test loaded a replacement engine that the application never loads and accepted a nonexistent defect identifier as the explanation for prohibited variance.
findings.basis: Specification section 37 Stage 13 requires prohibited variance to have an actual defect.
findings.correction: Removed the unused alternate engine, exercised the production gate with otherwise valid cases, corrected the production defect-reference check, and detected a bypassed gate.
findings.status: CORRECTED; INTEGRATED RECHECK PENDING

findings.defect: Timing fault detection only searched the source for the expected timing call.
findings.basis: Specification sections 4.3 and 37; current due tests determine verification work.
findings.correction: Execute the matrix and proof-relation owners, inspect actual tuples, bypass each timing filter in disposable production modules, and require the behavioral oracle to fail.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED BASELINE AND TWO FAULTS PASS

findings.defect: The test missed future final-product tests being reported as unstable before they had due run observations. It also omitted the case where an entire requirement has only future obligations; the application invented current outcomes and required a premature comparison.
findings.basis: Specification section 4.3 due-obligation rule.
findings.correction: Require stability keys to equal the due-test universe; production now filters to that universe; filter-removal fault detected. Derive a due-requirement subset from the actual verification relation set and use it in comparison, stability, corrected-iteration and confirmation consumers; keep all mandatory requirements registered. Add timing-change and filter-bypass component cases.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED DUE-TEST AND FUTURE-REQUIREMENT CASES PASS; FULL INTEGRATED RECHECK PENDING

findings.defect: Changing unaccepted run flags to COMPLETED was expected to establish ten materially independent accepted operations.
findings.basis: Specification section 4.2 permits 3/N only for materially independent accepted operations.
findings.correction: Count distinct accepted operations with validation, proposal and raw-response acceptance links; test unaccepted flags and duplicate verification rows.
findings.status: CORRECTED; INTEGRATED RECHECK PENDING

findings.defect: A contract-name string or attributableExternalSystem Boolean was expected to establish verified trusted time.
findings.basis: Specification sections 17.11 and 29.14 require actual accepted trusted-time evidence.
findings.correction: Unverified claims remain SOURCE_ASSERTED and untrusted; a production fault that promotes the claims is detected.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED CASES PASS; VERIFIED EXTERNAL TIME PATH NOT ESTABLISHED

findings.defect: Source matches, test names, literals and small component ratios were promoted into complete coverage and zero-failure acceptance metrics.
findings.basis: Specification acceptance requirements and user sections 8 and 12 require executed, identified cases and the complete mandatory universe.
findings.correction: Unknown complete-universe metrics remain null; actual component reports and ratios are separately labelled; the existing CI report no longer converts component Booleans into full coverage.
findings.status: UNSUPPORTED CLAIMS REMOVED; COMPLETE MANDATORY EVIDENCE STILL REQUIRED

findings.defect: A context assertion ended in || true and could not fail.
findings.basis: User section 8 requires tests to detect their intended failure.
findings.correction: Removed the tautology; actual per-prompt context checks remain.
findings.status: CORRECTED; ROUTE CASES PASS

findings.defect: Renaming an error-code string was reported as detection of bypassed byte-integrity enforcement. Other source mutations were also presented as runtime behavior proof.
findings.basis: Specification sections 4.3 and 19; user section 8 requires actual bytes and implementation-fault detection.
findings.correction: Declaration checks labelled as declarations; new production staging suite corrupts same-length stored bytes across all 30 stages, verifies specific rejection and repair, and detects bypassed production comparison.
findings.status: CORRECTED; 30 STAGING CASES AND COMPARISON FAULT PASS; STORAGE I/O IS A DOUBLE

findings.defect: A prerequisite helper restored downstream records and job pointers after upstream acceptance had invalidated them, masking dependency failures.
findings.basis: Specification revision/dependency rules and user replacement/history requirements.
findings.correction: Reject downstream-bearing setup; stop resurrecting downstream state; establish later product pointers after prerequisite setup.
findings.status: CORRECTED; COMPONENT PREREQUISITES REMAIN EXPLICITLY STIPULATED

findings.defect: Several invalid Test IR examples had no preceding operand and never demonstrated a valid repaired case. Selector-depth tests covered legacy authoring syntax while the canonical DAG validator accepted over-depth selectors.
findings.basis: Specification closed Test IR/resource contracts and user section 8.
findings.correction: Otherwise valid baseline/violation/repair pairs; specific diagnostics; both legacy and canonical selector paths; production canonical selector validation corrected.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED NEGATIVE/REPAIR PAIRS PASS

findings.defect: String(object) converted the next-action result to [object Object], so the negative text assertion could not inspect the actual action. Global helper/text bans also reached beyond the particular filename-only fixture. Stage 27 also required three synonymous phrases (optional, not required, non-gating), making concise correct wording fail.
findings.basis: Stage-appropriate required context must remain available; no unsupported global prohibition.
findings.correction: Inspect the actual serialized action; remove unsupported application-wide helper/text bans; retain the scoped filename-only fixture. Inspect structured values rather than String(object). Preserve observable optional-advisory behavior and remove the forced repetition from the test and interface.
findings.status: CORRECTED; INTEGRATED RECHECK PENDING

findings.defect: Only exact positive capability names were tested; production substring matching accepted NOT_CAD_TOOL and other unrelated claims as CAD_TOOL.
findings.basis: Specification section 23.2 requires the actual registered capability.
findings.correction: Otherwise identical wrong-name cases; exact production name or capability-ID matching.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED CASES PASS; EXTERNAL CAPABILITY EXECUTION NOT CLAIMED

findings.defect: CSS strings, dimensions, navigation checks, or no visual check were reported as preserved/approved visual-baseline evidence.
findings.basis: Required visual-baseline evidence is separate from CSS declarations and synthetic viewport checks.
findings.correction: Report the actual CSS/navigation/component scope and leave visual-baseline acceptance false.
findings.status: FALSE CLAIMS CORRECTED; EXACT DEPLOYED VISUAL ACCEPTANCE STILL REQUIRED

findings.defect: Unused writer emitted PROVEN, claimed listed fixtures had run, marked prior proofs replayed, and invented external-actor PASS entries from stage mappings and an environment flag.
findings.basis: Executed proof and independent/human/device observations cannot be inferred from names or flags.
findings.correction: Removed unused obsolete writer; retained historical reports as historical records.
findings.status: RETIRED; NO EXISTING CI INVOCATION REMOVED

findings.defect: A local release-eligibility helper duplicated a simplified rule used only by its own test, so it did not test the production release gate.
findings.basis: Specification physical-device acceptance and release-gate requirements.
findings.correction: Removed duplicate helper; exercise real evidence and submission validators with specific negative/repaired cases; preserve CI wiring checks as configuration evidence.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED SYNTHETIC VALIDATOR CASES PASS; NO PHYSICAL DEVICE CLAIM

findings.defect: Changed a copied fixture property and asserted that it differed, then reported mutation sensitivity; two different random samples were described as nonrepeatability.
findings.basis: User section 8 requires a fault to be detected by a relevant executed test.
findings.correction: Invoke the actual target generator with changed input, check bound fields, and report only the two observed distinct challenges.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED GENERATOR CASES PASS

findings.defect: Reported destinationBoundDecisionAccepted:true although every corresponding assertion expected false.
findings.basis: Evidence must describe the actual result.
findings.correction: Report rejection of generic destination claims and explicitly identify the suite as negative authority component cases.
findings.status: CLAIM CORRECTED; POSITIVE DEDICATED INTENT COVERED SEPARATELY

findings.defect: Prompt-contract enumeration was labelled allOperationsVerified, and isolated stage ingestion samples were labelled a 30/30 ingestion cycle.
findings.basis: Complete operator journeys require preceding operations and actual controls/file transport.
findings.correction: Expose executed stage/operation samples and prompt-contract counts; record the invoked ingestion suite; explicitly mark them as component evidence.
findings.status: CLAIMS CORRECTED; COMPLETE BROWSER JOURNEY STILL REQUIRED

findings.defect: The common negative-case helper did not first establish a valid baseline or prove repaired acceptance, allowing a second invalidity to mask the intended violation.
findings.basis: User section 8 requires otherwise valid deliberate violations and successful correction.
findings.correction: Common helper now validates baseline, checks the exact rejection code and unchanged accepted state, then validates and accepts the original corrected response; reports actual case IDs and codes.
findings.status: CORRECTED FOR COMMON HELPER; REMAINING BESPOKE NEGATIVE CASES REQUIRE INDIVIDUAL REVIEW

findings.defect: Source declarations and source-token mutations were used as evidence of runtime parser/state/worker behavior. Baseline and Stage 30 checks also called matching function names and UI identifiers evidence of working operator paths. Stage 03 operation declarations were reported as source-research operation closure.
findings.basis: User section 8 requires executed behavior and relevant implementation faults.
findings.correction: Execute actual contract, parser, reservation and worker protocol owners; run disposable dynamic-code faults; retain architecture checks with explicit declaration scope. Remove unsupported UI-wiring claims and source-only assertions; exercise terminal recalculation to check that it does not issue a terminal command. Label operation-registry checks as declarations and physical-device evidence as unestablished.
findings.status: SOURCE-ONLY CLAIMS CORRECTED; TARGETED COMPONENT EXECUTION AND FULL BROWSER ACCEPTANCE TRACKED SEPARATELY

findings.defect: Ledger negative tests accepted any thrown error as detection of their particular violation.
findings.basis: User section 8 requires rejection for the specific violation.
findings.correction: Check each exact ledger error class/message and successful restored validation; label metadata validation separately from application evidence.
findings.status: CORRECTED; EXECUTED CASES PASS

findings.defect: The contradiction loop asserted only that the detector returned an array; an empty array passed even when the intended conflict was absent.
findings.basis: Specification sections 26 and 31; user test-sensitivity requirement.
findings.correction: Replace the vacuous loop with a valid inspection, a single missing page/view observation, the exact conflict and record key, successful repair, and a detector-bypass fault. Label the retained malformed examples as smoke cases.
findings.status: CORRECTED; BASELINE, SPECIFIC CONFLICT, REPAIR AND BYPASS-FAULT CASES PASS

findings.defect: Multi-defect negative examples lacked valid evidence and did not expose the production acceptance of a favorable determination paired with an explicitly failed observation.
findings.basis: Controlled outcomes and consistent effective determinations; specification sections 26 and 31.
findings.correction: Add otherwise valid result-evaluator cases for verification, deterministic, meaning and adversarial results; reject the controlled outcome conflict, restore progression, preserve expected-negative outcomes and ordinary prose, detect bypassed enforcement. Correct the shared result adjudicator.
findings.status: CORRECTED FOR THE EXECUTED FOUR RESULT-EVALUATOR FAMILIES; NATIVE RESULT PATH AND COMPLETE EXTERNAL JOURNEYS ARE SEPARATE

findings.defect: A safe accented filename was required to fail solely because it was non-ASCII. Three host-normalization examples and invented character substitutions did not establish the mandated pinned Unicode contract.
findings.basis: Specification sections 17.11 and 29.14 require Unicode 15.1.0 NFC, default case folding and supported confusable collision keys.
findings.correction: Use bundled tables generated from digest-pinned Unicode 15.1.0 release data. Execute all 19,074 normalization cases, 1,530 folding mappings and 6,311 confusable mappings; retain unsafe-path/control rejection and detect normalization bypass. Bind deployment metadata to the actual table and source identities.
findings.status: CORRECTED; OFFICIAL DATA CORPUS AND DEPLOYMENT-MANIFEST CHECK PASS; PHYSICAL FILE TRANSPORT NOT CLAIMED

findings.defect: The stricter comparison repair initially selected earlier defect evidence through the latest iteration, preventing the actual correction path from continuing. The earlier focused test did not exercise that continuation.
findings.basis: Current iteration and dependency identity rules. This regression was introduced during this repair, not attributed to the starting application.
findings.correction: Preserve the failed stage-17 input state and action sequence; bind evidence to the comparison iteration; test continuation and detect reintroduction of the wrong-scope lookup.
findings.status: CORRECTED; FOCUSED REGRESSION AND SYNTHETIC COMMAND JOURNEY THROUGH 30 STAGES PASS; EXACT BROWSER JOURNEY PENDING

findings.defect: The report called a successful canonical hash calculation persistence checked after every operation. Hashability does not establish a durable save or recovery. With fixture export enabled, replacement cases were skipped but the report did not expose that scope.
findings.basis: User requirements 8 and 10 require executed, identified operations and honest synthetic/persistence evidence.
findings.correction: Report canonical serialization and explicitly mark durable persistence false; identify executed commands, stage gate checks, effective source hashes, replacement-case count, and re-executions requiring a new target.
findings.status: REPORT CORRECTED; LOCAL INTEGRATED RUN EXECUTED THE UPDATED COUNTERPART REPORT; CI 827 FAILED IN ITS STALE FAULT-DRIVER EXPECTATION (TEST-32)

findings.defect: The applicability test expects a fabricated ACCEPTED review with arbitrary author/reviewer strings and no current registered contexts, accepted review command or reviewed hash binding to remove a mandatory requirement.
findings.basis: Specification sections 26.5 and 26.7 require independent review for reductions and current proof/epistemic authority.
findings.correction: Require actual current registered independent author/reviewer contexts, a committed review response, a bound saved prompt and exact reviewed target hashes. Replace forged positive reviews in consuming fixtures with real author/reviewer ingestion operations. Preserve accepted APPLICABLE and NOT_APPLICABLE controls. Accepted records are not rehashed after an unrelated fixture setup.
findings.status: AUTHORITY COMPONENT REPAIRED; VALID CONTROLS, EIGHT SINGLE-VIOLATION CASES AND TWO IMPLEMENTATION FAULTS PASS; COMPLETE EXTERNAL REVIEW/RESERVATION DIMENSIONS REMAIN OPEN

findings.defect: A manually assigned SATISFIED proof-obligation flag was treated as sufficient conditional activation, without an actual accepted activation proof path.
findings.basis: Specification section 29 requires a conditional activation proof to obey the same current proof, evidence and review rules.
findings.correction: Require the actual linked activation proposition, expression, accepted proof review and computed truth. Replace fabricated positive controls with explicit UNKNOWN cases; detect bypassing activation validation.
findings.status: FALSE POSITIVE REMOVED; INVALID-ACTIVATION AND BYPASS COMPONENT CASES PASS; COMPLETE VALID CONDITIONAL-ACTIVATION JOURNEY NOT ESTABLISHED

findings.defect: Comparing Object.keys length with its Set size cannot find duplicate keys in an already constructed JavaScript object; the uniqueness assertion was a tautology.
findings.basis: Canonical collection paths must uniquely address the declared collections; user requirement to prove test sensitivity.
findings.correction: Check uniqueness of actual declared canonical JSON pointers and introduce duplicate production pointers in an isolated module.
findings.status: CORRECTED; VALID REGISTRY AND DUPLICATE-POINTER FAULT PASS

findings.defect: The order-independence positive fixture added an unreviewed file and rewrote an already inspected candidate, then required authorization under the old release. It also missed valid reversed paired artifact IDs/filenames being rejected. Metadata receipt checks were described as byte verification.
findings.basis: Specification sections 36.4, 36.5 and 36.8: identity joins by canonical ID/filename; changed candidate content invalidates inspection and later results.
findings.correction: Build a two-file product through the preceding synthetic production commands, test reversed input order, and reject changes to all eight candidate content categories. Correct paired-list mapping, frozen-content closure, and release binding. Keep actual byte-storage verification distinct from synthetic receipts.
findings.status: CORRECTED; VALID TWO-FILE COMMAND CONTROL AND 21 REJECTION CASES PASS; ORDER AND CANDIDATE-CONTENT BYPASS FAULTS DETECTED; BROWSER/STORED-BYTE ACCEPTANCE SEPARATE
findings.repairRegression: An initial repair included a displayed prerequisite status in release hashing. The existing Stage 27 idempotency test detected it; release and Stage 25 now share an inspection-record evaluator independent of displayed prerequisite status.

findings.defect: The fault driver expected an obsolete persistence-labelled assertion. The actual non-integer serialization fault was detected, but the wrapper rejected its correct error as unrelated, failing CI 827.
findings.basis: Fault tests must fail for the intended reason and report the actual mechanism exercised.
findings.correction: Require the specific canonical-number error and agreement-rate record path, then execute the restored valid 13-stage command control with replacement cases.
findings.status: CORRECTED; THREE INTENDED FAULTS DETECTED AND RESTORED COMMAND CONTROL PASSES

findings.defect: A manually seeded execution/evidence record was reported as an actual pre-correction product execution. An append-only schema declaration was reported as behavioral append-only enforcement.
findings.basis: Specification regression evidence requirements and user instruction to distinguish synthetic evidence from actual execution.
findings.correction: Retain the useful record-linkage gate cases but report stipulated synthetic execution records, declaration coverage, and actual product execution as unestablished.
findings.status: REPORT CORRECTED; RECORD-GATE COMPONENT CHECKS PASS; ACTUAL PRE-CORRECTION OPERATOR EXECUTION IS SEPARATE

findings.defect: Whole-stage prerequisite fixtures accept NO_APPLICABLE_EXTERNAL_SOURCE without the complete mandatory bounded source-search contract. Some omit it entirely; others omit the closed source-class checklist, stopping criteria and application-bound execution fields.
findings.basis: Specification section 8.3 explicitly requires one current bounded contract and successful criteria before NO_APPLICABLE_EXTERNAL_SOURCE. A literal-output project does not waive that procedure.
findings.correction: Open: correct the shared contract, execution/review authority and every consuming fixture; preserve legitimately bounded no-source decisions without inventing sources. Stage 03 protocol fixtures remain scalar/relationship component evidence only.
findings.status: CONFIRMED TEST/PRODUCTION COVERAGE DEFECT; COMPLETE REPAIR PENDING

findings.defect: The adjudication test prescribed exact source-code forms for shallow copying and cloning. Those text matches neither proved that recorded conclusions were preserved nor measured the required responsiveness; they could reject a different correct implementation.
findings.basis: The specification preserves original evidence and user requirements call for behavioral test sensitivity. It does not mandate these exact source strings.
findings.correction: Execute every stage gate with recorded conclusion claims in eleven families, compare the original fields after each call, inject shared mutable records, and require detection of the actual rewrite. Report workload latency separately as unestablished.
findings.status: CORRECTED; ALL 30 GATE CALLS PRESERVED THE ORIGINAL CONCLUSIONS, SHARED-RECORD FAULT DETECTED, RESTORED CONTROL PASSED

remainingReview: Complete predicate and fixture review of large browser, ingestion, full-cycle, lifecycle and semantic suites; no claim that every defective test has yet been found.
Run the stable integrated candidate through the existing complete CI and actual browser paths.
Validate the complete bounded source-search contract in Stage 2 and every consuming fixture; accepted abbreviated fixtures do not establish complete search adequacy.
Keep all 30 stages and all operation/recovery classes active; component repairs do not establish application completion.
Verify Unicode file selection/export/collision behavior in the actual browser and target device; table-level corpus results are not device evidence.
Complete valid conditional activation through actual producers, proof review and required evidence; a rejected success flag is not a valid activation journey.
Complete semantic-review reservation linkage and every required independence dimension; corrected current context/hash bindings are not the whole review specification.
